Sample preparation consisted of first grinding using SiC papers then a JEOL argon ion beam cross-sectional polisher was used to mill away the deformed layer leaving a small ~ 3 mm2 polished area. Large area EDS and BSE maps were collected on the polished region. This was done using an automated image acquisition workflow using Oxford AZTEC software, which used a rectangular grid ~ 1 mm wide and ~ 1.8 mm tall. A BSE image and EDS data were collected at each cell using a beam voltage of 20 kV, beam current of 100 (using analysis mode), 5 working distance of 10 mm, and 1000X magnification, which resulted in an EDS count rate of ~ 21k/s with a dead time of ~35%. EDS data was collected for 5 min per cell and cells overlapped by 20%. After all cells or field of views (FoVs) were captured then the BSE images and each EDS elemental map was stitched together using the AZTEC software. Fig. 1 (a) shows the large area BSE image of this alloy with dimension 0.634×0.948 mm2 in width and height, respectively. This image has 5022×7472 pixels and was obtained by stitching multiple 1000×? BSE images. In Fig. 1, the light color phase represents the second phase particles, and the rest is the Al- matrix. EDX scan of this area shows that the micron-scale particles contain Fe, Mn and Si and should be the Al9Fe2Si2 and Al12Mn phases, based on Thermo-Calc calculations (see Fig. 2). Fe and Mn may be exchangeable and these particles may be called iron-containing-particles or Fe-particles. The Cu content seems uniformly distributed in the material and there are some very small particles containing Mg which may be the Mg2Si. Image analysis of the SEM image using Matlab shows that there is around 0.83% volume fraction of the particles.
